s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
Lesions are itchy
Milia are present in the superficial dermis
Erosions with partially detached epidermis are present
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination shows dermoepidermal separation
Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, which is a known cause of this disease

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy, progressive skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia is consistent with this disease

shortlist.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic examination showing dermoepidermal separation is consistent with this disease, although genetic testing would be needed to confirm

shortlist.label: Kindler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia, combined with long-standing symptoms, makes this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of itchy, progressive skin lesions is consistent with this disease, although histopathologic examination and genetic testing would be needed to confirm

raw.rationale: The presence of milia in the superficial dermis and dermoepidermal separation on histopathologic examination, along with a novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1, are characteristic of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, a subtype of Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
rejected.why: The genetic testing and histopathologic findings are more consistent with a dystrophic form of epidermolysis bullosa rather than an acquired form.

rejected.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: The presence of milia and the specific genetic variant in COL7A1 are not characteristic of Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Kindler Syndrome
rejected.why: While Kindler Syndrome involves skin fragility, the specific combination of genetic and histopathologic findings in this case does not align with Kindler Syndrome.

rejected.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
rejected.why: Bullous Pemphigoid is an autoimmune disease that primarily affects the elderly, and the clinical and genetic findings in this case do not support this diagnosis.
